title: ABEDINOV v. "THE FORMER YUGOSLAV REPUBLIC OF MACEDONIA"
summary: In the case of Abedinov v. "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia," the applicant, Mr. Abedinov, identified as a member of the Roma community, brought a complaint against the Macedonian authorities. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers, focusing on alleged discrimination and restrictions on freedom of movement, issues that have historically affected these communities across Europe. Mr. Abedinov claimed that he had suffered discriminatory treatment and limitations on his right to liberty of movement, invoking several articles of the European Convention on Human Rights, including Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination), Article 2 of Protocol No. 4 (freedom of movement), and Article 1 of Protocol No. 12 (general prohibition of discrimination). Before the Court could issue a judgment on the merits, the parties reached a friendly settlement: the government agreed to pay Mr. Abedinov 2,500 euros to cover non-pecuniary damages and costs, with the payment to be made within three months. Satisfied that the settlement respected human rights, the Court struck the case from its list. This resolution is significant as it demonstrates the potential for amicable settlements in cases involving Roma rights, reflecting ongoing efforts to address longstanding patterns of discrimination and exclusion faced by Roma and Traveller communities in Europe.
